correctness.rationale: At N=3^h the denominator 2^N−1 is a 3-adic unit; summing the three refinements of each cylinder gives the previous weight by the geometric identity. The bounded compatible weights define the continuous integral. The finite generating-function difference from (2−e^z)⁻¹ has each n-th coefficient in exponential normalization divisible by N, yielding the exact moments in the limit. On units x²−1 belongs to 3Z_3, so ν_3(M_{ε,j})≥j and the Mahler series converge uniformly. The omitted nonunit moment is divisible by 3^n for n≥1, giving the required n≥k congruence. I independently recomputed the mod-81 coefficient rows [12,72,0,0] and [52,15,54,54] using normalized geometric weights and ordinary unit power moments. Vandermonde and ℓ binom(t−s,ℓ)=(t−s)binom(t−s−1,ℓ−1) give the difference bound ν_3(t−s)−floor(log_3 j). For j≥4 the coefficient valuation minus floor(log_3 j) is at least 3, and for j=2,3 the table gives at least 3 in the even branch and 2 in the odd branch. Thus only the linear term determines each exact distance. These distances give injection on the finite argument quotients of the appropriate size, hence surjection onto every reduction of the two balls, then onto the balls by compactness. All positive odd terms satisfy the base congruence mod 3 since n≥1, and all positive even terms satisfy their base congruence mod 9 since n≥2; F_0=1 lies in the odd ball. The two branch quotients give the single and triple fibers and arbitrarily late representatives. Reduction modulo 3 forces an even period, whose half is divisible by 3^{k−1} by odd-branch injectivity; k=1 is ordinary parity. The disjoint balls have Haar measure 1/3+1/9. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/1.py; it also checks the finite histograms and cyclic-period lengths through 3^5 using the independent recurrence F_n=Σ_{j<n} binom(n,j)F_j. These numerical tests do not replace the infinite arguments.
